source_snapshot.items: Network Validation Initial Environment Setup and trial run - Test Fabric Health
source_snapshot.procedure: Run IB-Stress between node-1 and node-2, run a new UFM Fabric Health report, then inspect UFM Alarms for `Fabric Health Report Warning` while Port RX Data Rate exceeds 100 Gb/s.
source_snapshot.criteria: The named UFM warning is generated when the condition is true.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL/CONFLICTING; preserves only generic UFM access and attaches unrelated subnet-merger risk, omitting load, threshold, report and alarm causality.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/CHANGED; restores exact load/threshold/report/alarm phases and requests timing/lifecycle evidence.

old_problem: The active review kept the source-specified 100-Gb/s threshold and alarm lifecycle pending. NVIDIA defines threshold-driven events/alarms and itemized Fabric Health reports; release labels, sampling intervals and delays are discoverable execution metadata. The authoritative trigger value and named warning already exist in the source.
disposition_reason: NVIDIA UFM documentation defines Fabric Health report execution and events/alarms when configured conditions are exceeded. The source explicitly sets Port RX Data Rate >100 Gb/s and expects Fabric Health Report Warning. ED-03 permits node/link/report bindings, ED-05 isolates IB load, ED-14 preserves the 15-minute allocation, ED-15 uses the approved threshold, and ED-17 preserves preexisting alarms. A synchronized threshold-crossing→report-ID→alarm timeline creates an auditable test without inventing criteria.
decision_basis: Directly read Compatibility row424 all 18 XLSX columns, same-row DeepSeek material, GPT V2/history3015, completed row423 baseline and adjacent row425 telemetry-curve case.
Applied NVIDIA UFM System Health and Events/Alarms behavior for itemized reports and threshold-triggered warning evidence.
Preserved the exact >100 Gb/s Port RX condition, named warning, Run New Report action and full 15-minute source allocation.
Required alarm prestate and unique report/time/link correlation so stale warnings cannot satisfy the case; no alarm acknowledgement or clearing is allowed.
Directly read next formal queue Compatibility row425 and verified its manifest identity; no traffic, report, alarm or fabric action ran.

test_case.test_name: 15-minute IB load to UFM >100-Gb/s Fabric Health warning causality
test_case.purpose: Prove a new UFM Fabric Health report observes the approved node-1/node-2 link above 100 Gb/s Port RX Data Rate and generates the exact corresponding Fabric Health Report Warning.
required_package: Approved UFM/version/account, fabric/node/link GUID/port identity and healthy baseline
Pinned finite two-node IB-Stress/perftest profile capable of the source threshold, with 900-second watchdog and safe abort
Confirmed UFM Port RX Data Rate metric, Gbit/s units, sampling/report window and synchronized clocks
Alarm/report export access, preexisting alarm snapshot and release-specific warning fields/lifecycle
test_case.test_command: Capture UFM/fabric/link identity, clocks, existing alarms and idle Port RX samples. Start the approved node-1/node-2 IB load for the complete 900-second allocation under a hard watchdog. Confirm the exact mapped UFM Port RX Data Rate produces timestamped samples >100 Gb/s; while true, invoke one System Health > Fabric Health > Run New Report. Preserve its unique report ID, selected checks, window and detail, then capture the newly created `Fabric Health Report Warning` with link, threshold, severity and timestamps. Stop traffic, retain post-condition samples/alarm lifecycle and verify fabric health.
test_case.expected_result: The mapped link crosses >100 Gb/s during the bounded load, the one new report covers that interval and records the condition, and exactly attributable new warning evidence appears with the expected name/link/threshold and valid timing. Traffic terminates and the link/fabric remain healthy; post-condition behavior follows documented UFM lifecycle without deleting evidence.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires full 900-second load evidence, timestamped >100-Gb/s samples in confirmed units, unique report ID/scope overlapping the crossing, a newly attributable named warning and clean post-health. A stale alarm, wrong link, threshold inferred from endpoint-only output, report outside the window or generic health-page status cannot pass.
safety_gate: Use only the approved isolated IB path and bounded 900-second traffic with external watchdog
Verify the mapped link has capacity/headroom to exceed 100 Gb/s and stop on errors, congestion outside scope or thermal/fabric limits
Snapshot alarms/reports before load; do not acknowledge, delete, clear logs or change event policy
Abort on identity/unit/time mismatch, unexpected alarm, link degradation or management loss; stop both peers and never auto-retry
expected_evidence: UFM/fabric/node/link identity, versions, clocks and alarm/report baseline
Exact supervised traffic commands, 900-second timeline, outputs/status and endpoint counters
UFM Port RX samples proving >100 Gb/s with metric/unit/link identity
Fabric Health report ID, scope/window/detail and real UI screenshot
New warning name/link/threshold/severity/timestamps, lifecycle, post-health and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: On any load, report or alarm anomaly, stop both traffic peers, preserve the full threshold/report/alarm timeline, restore only temporary network state from the approved traffic case and verify link/UFM/fabric health. Do not clear or acknowledge alarms, rerun the report or restart traffic automatically.

blocked.reason: The source supplies threshold and expected warning; release/runtime identity and timing are bindable parameters.
